what_happened: On an open multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no visible reason (21.9 → 5.9 m/s, with the nearest lead more than 40 m away), so actor 1 in the left lane caught up and drew alongside. The ego's planned path then bent left and its front hit actor 1 as that car passed on the left. The ego was also rear-ended by traffic behind it.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard from about 20 to 8 m/s with no lead nearby (the nearest was about 48 m ahead). Actor 1 in the left lane kept its speed and pulled ahead. Meanwhile the ego's plan bent left into that lane, and the ego cut across the lane line and hit actor 1's rear-right corner with its front. The phantom braking probably also caused the separate rear-end contact from behind.

On a clear multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard after handoff (20.6 to 7.6 m/s) with no lead vehicle close (gap about 48 m or none). Actor 1 in the left lane overtook it, and the ego's planned path veered left into that lane, so the ego's front-left corner struck actor 1. The rear-end contact recorded for this run happened after that collision and was likely caused by the unneeded braking.

On an open multi-lane highway with no close lead (gap over 40 m), the ego braked hard for no clear reason, from 23.7 to 7.5 m/s. While slowing, it drifted left toward the adjacent lane, where actor 1 was coming up from behind-left. The ego's front hit actor 1's side as the two came alongside.

Unprompted hard braking on an open highway: after handoff the ego slowed from 18.6 to 5 m/s with nothing close ahead (the lead was about 48 m away) and drifted about 1.6 m left of the recorded path. Actor 28, a replayed car that had been following on the recorded path and does not react to the ego, caught up and struck the ego's right side (and rear).

On an open highway, the ego braked hard for no visible reason. It slowed from 18 to 4.4 m/s while the nearest vehicle ahead in its lane stayed 43–57 m away, and it fell far behind the recorded trajectory (20.8 m). Actor 28, which was following the recorded path in the ego's lane, came up from behind. Because the ego had drifted slightly left, actor 28 struck it along the right front and side, so the contact was scored as an at-fault front collision even though the ego was also rear-ended.

The ego was speeding up from 3.5 to 7 m/s in dense multi-lane traffic. Its planned path (orange) bent left toward actor 15's lane, so it drifted about 1.5 m left of the recorded trajectory, onto the lane line, and side-swiped actor 56 in the adjacent left lane. The route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, so the left move went against it.

The ego was going straight in its highway lane with no vehicle ahead, slowing gently from 8.8 to 7.6 m/s, and fell about 20 m behind where the human car was at that point. Actor 24 came up from behind in the right lane, moved left into the ego's lane at 9.2 s and hit the ego's front-right corner. In the real drive that actor probably merged into a gap behind the faster human car, so this looks like a replayed actor that doesn't react to the ego, plus the ego's unexplained slowdown.

On a clear multi-lane highway with no close lead (the gap was more than 40 m or empty), the policy braked hard from 23.7 to 7.1 m/s and drifted left out of its lane. Its front-left corner hit actor 1, which had been behind it in the left lane and was passing the slowing ego.

On a clear multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard for no visible reason, slowing from 23.7 to 7.1 m/s with the nearest vehicle ahead 43 m or more away. As it slowed, it drifted about 1.2 m left toward the adjacent lane. Actor 1, coming up from behind in that lane, drew alongside, and the ego's front-left touched it (an at-fault front collision; a rear contact was also flagged).

The ego was going straight and steady in its highway lane at about 8 m/s, roughly 20 m behind where the recorded car was at that point. Actor 24 came up from behind in the right lane, moved left into the ego's lane and struck the ego's right-front corner; there was no lead vehicle, and the ego kept to its lane.

With no lead vehicle, the ego braked hard on an open highway (18.6 to 5.1 m/s) and drifted about 1.6 m left of the recorded path, toward the lane behind actor 1. Actor 28 was following in the ego's original lane, replaying the recorded drive. It caught up with the now much slower ego, which still straddled the lane, and side-swiped its right side. Some actor also hit the ego's rear.

After handoff on an open highway, the ego braked hard for no visible reason, slowing from 16.9 to 5.5 m/s with no lead vehicle within about 50 m, while the recorded human kept going (the ego was 20 m behind the human's position by the end). Non-reactive traffic following the recorded speed caught up: the ego had already been rear-ended, and at 7.6 s actor 28 came up alongside on the right and overlapped the ego, which counts as a front/side collision.
